role: conditional aggregate-energy feasibility bound for the unchanged full-capacity service product; no controller search
registration_context: four causal-service pilot outcomes observed: both admitted runs finish physically but have 95 capacity-shortfall hours and 58 partial requests; raw runs fail at minutes 430 and 445; direction-count and aggregate-energy prefix bounds unobserved

scope.request_marks: all 168 existing hourly marks, unchanged; do not regenerate, drop, reorder or resize requests
scope.pulse: one-minute ramp, 30-minute hold, one-minute return; net peak 98 MW under a full-service common-direction call
scope.firm_obligation: both directional offers must deliver the complete 49 MW per unit at every hourly clock, including no-activation clocks
scope.physical_model: two independent 98 MWh stocks; 0.92 charging and discharging efficiency; no energy input except PN and the prescribed accepted calls
scope.information: hourly pulses do not overlap; no accepted pulse remains active at the next hourly declaration
scope.no_retuning: retain all pilot controls, calls, obligations and negatives; the bound does not fit another capacity or target

procedure: Let M_i=max of the two locked PN slots and m_i=min. Full joint export peaks M_i+49 require sum(M_i)<=0, and full joint import peaks m_i-49 require sum(m_i)>=0 at an exact 98 MW gross limit. Since M_i>=m_i, both sums are zero and each unit's locked PN is constant over its hour. Therefore summed PN power is zero under exact full service.
With the retained 1e-8 MW power tolerance, the same inequalities bound every PN and pulse net-power deviation from the ideal zero-baseline pulse by 1e-8 MW; do not increase the tolerance.

Conversion losses mean zero-net-power PN cannot increase total stock. For each ideal net-export pulse total stock decreases by at least its net energy divided by 0.92; for each net-import pulse stock increases by at most 0.92 times its net energy.

Use ramp-inclusive ideal site energy: at pulse age s minutes the peak-equivalent area is s^2/2 for 0<=s<=1, s-0.5 for 1<=s<=31, 30.5+(s-31)-(s-31)^2/2 for 31<=s<=32, and 31 thereafter; multiply by 98/60 MWh.

At every integer minute from 0 through 10080 compute the generous total-stock upper bound U=98+0.92*ideal_net_import_MWh-ideal_net_export_MWh/0.92+(1e-8/0.92)*elapsed_hours. Keep this upper bound uncapped at 196 MWh; ignoring overflow and circulation losses makes it more generous.

If U is below minus twice the retained 1e-8 MWh unit-stock tolerance at any inspected minute, the literal full-service obligation is infeasible for every PN policy satisfying these hypotheses. Retain the first inspected violating minute and prefix import/export counts. If no such minute exists, the bound is inconclusive and does not certify feasibility.
report: a short analytic derivation, one compact prefix CSV, summary of the first bound violation or inconclusive result; no new simulated controller traces
decision: a violated bound directs work to the business-duty and capacity specification before more controller search; an inconclusive bound directs work to per-unit stock and delayed-PN scheduling. Neither branch changes the 49 MW pilot obligation or advances source comparison.
limitations: conditional necessity bound for this constructed hourly full-capacity bidirectional service product only; not an impossibility claim for real BM operation, other duties or all online battery policies, and not an OR submission readiness certificate
